parsed.summary: Mispaired: paper Lemma 8.7 is about choosing five bump profiles so that an axisymmetric increment (∆v, γd) uniquely solves the integral constraints (8.25). The Lean theorem is an unrelated torus-averaging identity. It says that the square-average over z of the angular mean of a(z)·cos²(jθ+phase(z)) equals (|det(vr,vt)|/2)·(∫χ²)·actualColumn_i, where a is a periodized native slot field composed with an n-fold covering map. Most components (periodize, nativeField, slotChart, transverseStretch, pulseProfile, squareAverage, covering, period) are not visible, so even the Lean statement's own meaning cannot be fully checked.

glossary.plain: Vector with i-th entry ci·∫_ℝ ψ(v)²·x(v)·t(v)_i dv.
glossary.note: Bespoke. The integrand is integrable here because ψ is compactly supported and ψ, x, t are continuous, so the junk value 0 does not arise.
`period` is not shown. The theorem uses SmoothLoop.angularMean, and it is not visible whether that is this definition.
Not used by the theorem: it is shadowed by the local `let a` on line 39.

glossary.plain: Slot center plus a lattice point.
glossary.note: The theorem takes `center` as an arbitrary Plane parameter, which shadows this definition.

lean_claims.plain: Hypotheses: vectors vr, vt with det(vr,vt) ≠ 0; any center; ci > 0 and any r0; χ, ψ, x, t continuous; χ and ψ compactly supported; i ∈ Fin 2; n ∈ ℕ; any phase function; integer j ≠ 0. Let a(z) be the periodization of the native field of the transverse-stretched pulse profile in the slot chart, evaluated at covering^[n](z). Conclusion: squareAverage_z of angularMean_θ[a(z)·cos²(jθ+phase z)] = (|det|/2)·∫χ²·actualColumn(ci,ψ,x,t)_i.

paper_claims.plain: Assume the slow base satisfies (8.24) with λ > 0 and |a(η)| ≥ a0 > 0. Then there are three azimuthal and two axial bump profiles such that, for arbitrary targets (P, Jθ, Jz), a unique linear combination (∆v, γd) satisfies the five integral constraints (8.25). The resulting increments are linear in the targets, lie in the stated classes, and preserve the integral constraints.

coverage.why: mispaired: the Lean statement is a torus/angular averaging identity for periodized slot coefficients; the paper's Lemma 8.7 concerns invertibility of a bump-profile system for axisymmetric increments (8.25). They share only the label.

flags.explanation: The paper Lemma 8.7 shown is a different result, so the docstring's citation refers to a candidate-manuscript numbering. Nothing in the published Lemma 8.7 is formalized by this declaration.

Key definitions are not visible: periodize, nativeField, slotChart, transverseStretch, pulseProfile, squareAverage, covering, SmoothLoop.angularMean and period. Also, a(z) does not depend on θ, so the angular mean reduces to a(z)·(average of cos²). That average is 1/2 only if period is a multiple of 2π (or of π/|j|); the theorem's content depends on this hidden constant.
The LHS is built from a ℂ-valued angular mean, while the RHS is a real product. The equality involves an implicit cast whose direction depends on squareAverage's signature, which is not shown.
